page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, translating to a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at 2.7 GHz. This hardware configuration consists of 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The processor includes a substantial 105 MB L3 cache, alongside 2 MB L2 and 48 KB L1d caches. It supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for vector and matrix operations, as well as hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES and SHA-NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data reveals moderate single-core performance alongside weaker multi-core scaling. The instance achieves average ratings in single-core stress-ng (1618.89) and Geekbench single-core (1713.0) tests. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 3813.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 3315.66. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with read-only large block bandwidth at 28.42 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 21.13 GB/sec, both falling into the lower performance tiers. Similarly, Passmark database operations (2014.12) and software compilation benchmarks are weak. Conversely, the instance demonstrates average throughput in static web serving (6.68 GB/sec) and single-threaded gzip compression (26.37 GB/sec).

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c3-standard-4 offers a balanced resource density suitable for entry-level enterprise workloads that do not demand high memory bandwidth or intensive multi-core parallelization. The inclusion of dedicated Intel Xeon cores with AMX and AVX-512 provides specialized execution capabilities for lightweight vector math and cryptography without the overhead of a GPU. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and the modest memory bandwidth make it less optimal for high-throughput database systems or large-scale data processing. The instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, basic text processing, lightweight single-threaded applications, and moderate utility computing.
